skill.name: ccxt-python
skill.description: CCXT cryptocurrency exchange library for Python developers. Covers both REST API (standard) and WebSocket API (real-time). Helps install CCXT, connect to exchanges, fetch market data, place orders, stream live tickers/orderbooks, handle authentication, and manage errors in Python. Use when working with crypto exchanges in Python projects, trading bots, data analysis, or portfolio management. Supports both sync and async (asyncio) usage.
skill.summary: Reference guidance for Python exchange integrations using CCXT REST APIs, WebSocket streams, authentication, and order routing.
skill.author: ccxt

security_audit.summary: All 419 static findings are false positives involving Markdown, reference URLs, proxy placeholders, exchange authentication, or financial API terminology. Two documentation risks remain: live routing without spending or freshness limits, and raw diagnostics without redaction guidance. No evidence found of prompt injection, hidden command execution, or intentional credential exfiltration in the reviewed file.

remediation.issue: The live routing example omits notional and plan-age limits.
remediation.suggestion: Keep examples in dry-run mode unless live execution is necessary. Every live example should set positive maxNotionalUsd and maxPlanAgeMs limits and require user approval.

remediation.issue: Debugging examples print raw exchange responses without privacy guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Use public endpoints for diagnostics and redact credentials, balances, and order details before logging or sharing. Disable verbose logging after troubleshooting.

content.user_title: Build Python Exchange Integrations with CCXT
content.value_statement: Cryptocurrency exchanges expose different APIs for market data, account access, and trading. This skill guides Python integrations through CCXT examples for REST requests and WebSocket streams.
actual_capabilities: Explain CCXT installation and synchronous or asynchronous exchange initialization.
Provide REST examples for tickers, order books, balances, orders, and trade history.
Guide real-time ticker, order book, trade, and account subscriptions with CCXT Pro.
Explain environment-based authentication, rate limiting, capability checks, and exchange error handling.
Describe order-router queries, dry runs, execution plans, idempotency, and optional safety limits.
Document prediction-market outcome handles and Bitget stock-routing distinctions.
limitations: This is a documentation skill, not a bundled trading service; CCXT installation and exchange access are separate requirements.
Method availability, permissions, market limits, and exchange behavior must be checked for each integration.
Some reference sections contain JavaScript syntax and camelCase examples that need adaptation for Python.
The documented Python order router is synchronous and does not implement watch_route streaming.

use_cases.description: Combine authenticated balance subscriptions with live market streams for account monitoring without enabling order placement.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: Fetch a public ticker
prompt_templates.prompt: Show a synchronous Python CCXT example that loads Binance markets and fetches BTC/USDT. Enable rate limiting and use no credentials or trading methods.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: Stream market updates
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an asyncio CCXT Pro ticker monitor for BTC/USDT and ETH/USDT. Check exchange support, handle network errors, and close connections in finally blocks.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: Monitor private balances
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a read-only Python balance monitor using named environment variables. Check permissions, handle authentication failures, and keep secrets and account details out of logs.

prompt_templates.title: Expert: Review a router execution plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Python order-router dry run with a stable request identity, positive notional and plan-age limits, and unknown-outcome handling. Do not enable live execution.

output_examples.input: Explain how to choose between REST and WebSocket access for a market dashboard.
output: REST suits initial snapshots and occasional queries.
CCXT Pro WebSocket subscriptions suit continuous ticker and order book updates.
Check method support and close asynchronous connections during shutdown.

output_examples.input: Review the safety requirements before testing a CCXT router plan.
output: Start with dry-run execution and validate market rules.
Set a positive spending cap and reject stale plans.
Use a stable request identity and reconcile uncertain outcomes before retrying.
Require explicit approval before any live order placement.

best_practices: Use narrowly scoped exchange credentials from environment variables and redact all shared diagnostics.
Check exchange capabilities and market limits; enable rate limiting and close asynchronous clients in finally blocks.
Test with dry runs or supported sandboxes; require approval, spending limits, freshness checks, and stable identities before live trading.
anti_patterns: Paste real API secrets into prompts, source files, or diagnostic logs.
Run live order examples without approval, spending limits, or market validation.
Retry an order with an unknown outcome before checking the venue for an existing order or fill.

faq.question: Does this skill install CCXT automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides installation commands and integration guidance. Package installation remains a separate action.

faq.question: Are API keys required for market data?
faq.answer: Many public market-data methods need no credentials. Private balances, orders, and account streams generally require exchange API credentials.

faq.question: How do REST and WebSocket usage differ?
faq.answer: REST supports individual requests. CCXT Pro provides asynchronous WebSocket subscriptions for continuous updates where the exchange supports them.

faq.question: Does every exchange support the listed methods?
faq.answer: No. Check exchange capabilities, required permissions, market rules, and the installed CCXT version before using a method.

faq.question: Can these examples place real orders?
faq.answer: Yes, authenticated trading examples can affect real funds. Use dry runs or supported sandboxes and require approval before live execution.

faq.question: Can the Python order router stream routes?
faq.answer: The guide states that watch_route raises NotSupported in Python. The documented router client is synchronous.
